summary.prose: Development installation resolves the chosen repository/branch to an accepted commit, builds it with verified private tooling and publishes a complete immutable release. The existing manager retains operation ownership and the shared terminal retains prompts/TUI handoff. This revision specifies the S1 integration seams, durable source checkout, receipt reopening and explicit pre-publication recovery exposed by the completed foundation. [[c1]] [[c3]] This revision records the user's explicit owned/cooperating actor cleanup boundary; it does not promise arbitrary descendant containment.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a1: one shared user-level installer/manager with bundle and dev delivery adapters. Install launched from either IDE runs the same public platform installer script interactively in a visible terminal; the script owns prompts and output. IDE-specific installation wizards and hidden background installs are excluded. Lifecycle, migration, runtime and privilege constraints remain shared and unchanged. Successful interactive installation hands the same terminal directly to the installed insrc TUI after daemon readiness; it does not finish at an idle shell.

consumedContracts.name: Installation and release identity
consumedContracts.purpose: One installation owns one selected delivery mode, zero or one active release and zero or one unresolved operation. Release identities are immutable; the controller metadata never stores application DB contents.

consumedContracts.name: Manager command and operation state
consumedContracts.purpose: A private-runtime command runner serves both IDEs when daemon is running, stopped or blocked. One OS-backed exclusive lock serializes all mutating operations per installation; controller records and bounded progress are shared across clients. Interactive install is invoked by the shared script in the terminal. The structured manager protocol remains for ordinary control/status; the IDE does not drive installation prompts through it. The 'install' action is reserved exclusively for the shared bootstrap/installer script executing inside the interactive terminal. VS Code/JetBrains adapters must never invoke ManagerAction.install directly or drive its prompts through this protocol; they only launch/focus the terminal and observe completion/readiness. The s1 LLD must state and enforce this caller restriction.

consumedContracts.name: Dependency report and consent
consumedContracts.purpose: Foundation contract separates required private Node, Ollama availability and advisory agent CLI detection from their platform implementations in s3; IDEs cannot infer consent from plugin updates.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface DependencyReport { runtimeReady: boolean; ollama: 'ready' | 'installed-not-running' | 'missing' | 'unavailable'; ollamaInstallOffer?: { id: string; destination: string; version: string }; agents: { claude: boolean; codex: boolean; vibe: boolean }; recommendations: string[]; blockers: string[] }
interface DependencyDecision { offerId: string; choice: 'install' | 'decline' }

consumedContracts.name: Ordered upgrade hook delegation
consumedContracts.purpose: Owned by foundational s1 because delivery preparation, startup guard and s5 runner all require the same hook manifest. s5 implements execution. Hooks run in-process inside a candidate daemon migration-only process that exclusively owns data; manager and IDE never open LMDB/Lance.

consumedContracts.name: Local transport and explicit installation home
consumedContracts.purpose: All consumers resolve the same installation home and endpoint. Unix retains daemon.sock; Windows uses a per-user/per-installation named pipe. The manager's Node bridge supplies JetBrains Windows transport without changing application RPC payloads.

boundary.internal: Private dev checkout/branch sync, lockfile installation and native build preparation; returns the same immutable prepared candidate. It does not define a second lifecycle or migration engine. Include the selected release's installed TUI entry/assets in the payload and default successful interactive installer-to-TUI handoff. adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own the foundational manifest, controller/operation/consent/hook/transport contracts because every branch already depends on s1. Private implementation covers bootstrap, runtime/payload integrity, bundle preparation/publication, platform lock adapter and atomic install records. Later stories implement lifecycle, checks and hooks behind these contracts. The canonical scripts and interactive installer mode are shared with manual invocation and both IDEs; terminal prompts and durable results are part of this foundation. Include the selected release's installed TUI entry/assets in the payload and default successful interactive installer-to-TUI handoff. The s1 LLD must explicitly reserve ManagerAction.install to the shared terminal bootstrap script and forbid IDE-adapter invocation. No delivery sync/build on start and no signal/PID daemon control. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S004:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private ordered migration runner, daemon migration-only mode, blocked-state persistence, interrupted-run validation and explicit retry. Hooks alone choose data changes and recovery policy. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S005:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private VS Code native terminal open/focus/launch integration, duplicate-action handling and post-install reconnect. It invokes the shared script and leaves all install prompts/output in that terminal, including after failure. Existing ordinary lifecycle and upgrade-consent UI remains thin. Successful installation automatically enters the installed TUI in that same terminal; the IDE only reconnects/status-checks and does not require a second click. Private JetBrains native terminal open/focus/launch integration with the same script, stdin/output and post-install readiness behavior as VS Code; no independent wizard or hidden install. Preserve background activation/control and Windows IPC bridge for ordinary daemon operations. Successful installation automatically enters the installed TUI in that same terminal; the IDE only reconnects/status-checks and does not require a second click. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S007:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private isolated VM/runner fixtures, target matrix evidence and release qualification results, including real Windows named-pipe behavior and preservation of host v2 daemon. Terminal-install parity checks cover each IDE and manual invocation, paths with spaces/Unicode, missing terminal support, declined Ollama, Ctrl+C/close, duplicate windows, retained output and readiness-confirmed completion. Verify successful install enters TUI in the original terminal, install lock is released before TUI use, TUI exit leaves daemon running, and failure/cancellation never opens TUI. nonFunctional.performance: Targets: local read-only inspection/reachability <=3 seconds; activation never blocks IDE UI. Progress/phase changes emit within 1 second after state changes. Ready startup target <=15 seconds excluding dependency/model initialization; startup probe deadline 30 seconds. Default graceful wait 60 seconds with configurable user deadline; timeout reports uncertainty and never silently escalates. Downloads/builds/hooks have per-operation budgets and progress, not an arbitrary task retry loop.
nonFunctional.security: No elevated commands, global PATH edits, user credential capture, LLM calls for dependency detection or shell-interpolated actions. Verify payload/runtime digests and targets, reject archive traversal/symlink escapes and module paths outside candidate payload. Local endpoints are user-scoped, capability-protected where needed; bind operation/instance/release identity. Signing deferred and no cryptographic authenticity claim from unsigned digest metadata. No IDE prompt automation or credential/input capture; terminal launch preserves argument boundaries. User-visible script identity matches manual release assets.
nonFunctional.observability: Structured operationId/installationId/from-to identity, platform/runtime/digest, phase/hook/stage, duration and actionable error code. Bounded NDJSON to IDE, logs in installation home with rotation; no credentials/tokens or full migration data. Report explicitly which platform/native checks passed and which were unavailable. Interactive installation prints human-readable phases and errors directly in the terminal. The terminal is retained after completion/failure; its output is not scraped or treated as success evidence.
nonFunctional.durability: OS-backed mutation exclusivity plus atomic versioned controller records. Prepared payloads immutable; candidate data mutation is daemon-owned only. Record hook run-started before execution and require test before completion; failures/interruption retain blocked startup. Retry never substitutes a different candidate or starts the predecessor after data changes automatically. Installation completion and lock release precede the interactive TUI session. TUI exit/launch failure cannot roll back the completed installation or keep an installation lock held.

dataModelChanges.entity: Dev source offer and accepted preparation checkpoint
dataModelChanges.details: Proposed source files: src/installer/dev.ts and src/installer/dev-worker.ts; these are new implementation locations, while callSites below are existing composition boundaries. One installation owns at most one unfinished controller operation; that operation owns exactly one accepted source offer and zero or more serial preparation attempts. Manager-owned dev-preparation metadata is stored under install/operations/<operationId>, with schema version, exact source offer, predecessor, attemptId/nonce, checkoutRelativePath, stageRelativePath, coordinator run identity and outcome. Persist accepted identity before launch admission. Candidate ID is not an assertion of publication. A preparation worker owns only its checkout/stage/results and never a controller writer or application data lease. No new public Phase/ManagerAction is added. [[c1]] [[c6]] [[c13]]
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff:
interface PreparationContext { operationId: string; signal?: AbortSignal; readCheckpoint(): DevPreparationRecord | undefined; checkpoint(record: DevPreparationRecord): void }
interface DevPreparationRecord { schemaVersion: 1; installationId: string; operationId: string; sourceOffer: DevSourceOffer; predecessorId?: string; attemptId: string; workerNonce: string; checkoutRelativePath: string; stageRelativePath: string; coordinatorRunId?: string; stage: 'accepted' | 'building' | 'prepared' | 'failed' | 'cancelled'; resultRelativePath?: string }

dataModelChanges.details: Each attempt allocates a new private checkout at <home>/dev/checkouts/<attemptId>; payload staging stays in <home>/install/staging/<operationId>-<attemptId>. The selected dev receipt points to exactly one managed checkout through a bounded contained relative path; the checkout belongs to that source preparation and is outside the immutable payload/inventory. At later dev upgrade, inspect that exact checkout: expected origin, detached HEAD/source commit, clean tracked/untracked/conflict state, and build-input fingerprint recorded after successful preparation. Build-generated ignored outputs are excluded using the accepted source's normal Git rules, not blanket exclusion of user files. A configured local source path is also inspected for dirty/conflicting work before fetch. Never reset/clean/modify the selected checkout; use a fresh attempt. Dirty/missing/foreign source gives an actionable error. After activation the new receipt chooses its retained checkout; former checkouts are preserved with no automatic GC. Failed/cancelled attempts delete only their proven-owned pristine staging after all actors close; changed or ownership-uncertain checkout data is retained for the user. [[c1]] [[c6]] [[c13]]

Cleanup is guaranteed for installer-admitted command actors, retained owned process groups and cooperating registered descendants. Arbitrary unregistered detached processes are outside this guarantee; it is an ownership contract, not process isolation. Known held/unknown owned actors, missing or mismatched registered-actor journals and unsupported tracked-actor disposal evidence remain preparation-uncertain and block publication, retry and cleanup. User decision: guarantee owned-process cleanup only. The private preparation worker uses the existing coordinator/process ownership pattern and writes a bounded nonce/source/attempt/run-bound result only after its command actors are confirmed closed; it has no publication callback or controller handle. A matching result, confirmed cleanup and released coordinator/worker ownership together permit manager verification/publication; a free operation lock, absent endpoint, PID/age, log line or result projection alone does not. Parent abort or terminal EOF cancels worker work and drains retained preparation actors within the configured budget. If the manager exits, a surviving worker may finish/dispose and persist its private result, but cannot publish/select/activate. Explicit same-operation retry-migration in preparing first checks checkpoint identities and prior actor closure. It can verify/finalize an already prepared stage, or create a new serial attempt for the same accepted source after a confirmed failed/cancelled attempt. A source ref is never re-resolved during recovery. Missing/contradictory evidence remains preparation-uncertain with retained diagnostics; no duplicate worker, automatic stage deletion, automatic retry loop or predecessor restart. The narrow window with an admitted worker but no positive outcome remains uncertain rather than guessed. Once publication is verified, the manager persists the usual candidate record; post-publication recovery continues through S1's existing exact-candidate path. Worker launch input and cancel frames are bounded/versioned and bind the operation/attempt/nonce; EOF is cancellation. Result/cleanup/child-close journal paths are derived from validated checkpoint IDs under the owned checkout, never accepted as arbitrary paths from output. A result is usable only with matching source/run identity, cleanup digest, confirmedClosed=true, observed close entries for all admitted command actors and released coordinator/worker ownership; status strings or exit-code projection alone are insufficient. Worker control/result schema is private preparation plumbing, not an IDE or daemon protocol. No workload or payload writes are admitted after a finalized result. [[c1]] [[c6]] [[c13]] The manager retains blocked/interrupted-preparing plus the checkpoint when child cleanup is unconfirmed, even though the daemon was never quiesced; it must not take the ordinary pre-disruption error path that clears the operation. Confirmed failed/cancelled preparation can finish without changing predecessor selection or its prior ready/stopped result. Explicit recovery requires the same operation ID; normal start/upgrade remains denied while ownership is uncertain. [[c6]] [[c13]]

dataModelChanges.entity: Dev receipt and immutable payload identity
dataModelChanges.details: One immutable release has exactly one receipt mode: qualified bundle .release.json or local .dev-release.json. A dev receipt binds one accepted source offer, one final sc1 manifest, one inventory and one managed checkout pointer; it is not a qualification record or migration journal. Receipt canonical bytes determine descriptorSha256, inventory bytes determine inventorySha256 and dev payloadSha256, and neither record hashes itself. Publication excludes both metadata files from inventory self-membership and rejects any extra receipt. Reopening validates full payload/runtime and actual manifest/offer identity independently in a new process. S1 bundle descriptors, archive-digest semantics and all external sc1/sc2 shapes are preserved. [[c1]] [[c6]] [[c13]]

errorCases.scenario: Configured source/ref or accepted offer changes
errorCases.detection: Parse repository form and git check-ref-format before argument-array execution; ls-remote returns one exact branch SHA, and locked re-resolution/offer digest comparison differs from the accepted ID.
errorCases.response: source-invalid/source-fetch-failed/offer-stale; require fresh explicit acceptance. After acceptance fetch only the pinned commit or report it unavailable; never use a replacement branch tip.
errorCases.userImpact: No source execution or incumbent disruption for an unaccepted revision.

errorCases.scenario: Dirty, conflicting, missing or foreign managed source
errorCases.detection: Resolve the selected dev receipt's contained checkout path, compare origin/HEAD/fingerprint and inspect porcelain status/unmerged entries, including untracked user files. Also inspect an explicitly selected local source working tree.
errorCases.response: source-dirty/source-conflict/source-identity-mismatch with the preserved checkout location; never reset, clean, switch branch or silently allocate a replacement for a missing selected tree.
errorCases.userImpact: All user edits and incumbent runtime remain usable and unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: Missing or mismatched private build toolchain
errorCases.detection: Verified Node/npm/header identity/target differs from release policy, required source-build helpers/lockfile are absent, or compiler/Git/extraction probe fails.
errorCases.response: runtime-invalid/source-prerequisite-missing/source-incompatible before lifecycle handoff; provide concrete user-level prerequisites, never elevation or host Node/npm fallback.
errorCases.userImpact: No false install/upgrade success or privileged modification.

errorCases.detection: Owned command exits nonzero, reaches deadline, changes source fingerprints or produces incomplete/unsafe payload bytes or failed target-native probes.
errorCases.response: source-build-failed; drain owned actors, persist exact attempt diagnostics, clean only proven-owned pristine staging, preserve selected source/release and report no activation.
errorCases.userImpact: Incumbent keeps serving; failed preparation does not select a partial release.

errorCases.scenario: Terminal cancellation or manager exits before candidate publication
errorCases.detection: AbortSignal/worker-control cancel or owner stdin EOF requests cancellation; manager restart sees a preparing checkpoint without ordinary candidate metadata.
errorCases.response: Propagate cancellation into owned process scope and await bounded confirmed child closure. Explicit retry-migration reconciles the same accepted source/attempt result, then finalizes verified prepared bytes or begins one fresh serial attempt. Missing cleanup, mismatched nonce or held/unknown actor ownership returns preparation-uncertain; no duplicate workers or automatic retries.
errorCases.userImpact: Cancellation prevents later publication/TUI handoff; interrupted work retains useful diagnostics and explicit recovery rather than guessing completion.

errorCases.detection: Recovered checkpoint names the expected release but the candidate record is missing, or a published directory exists without its matching durable operation projection.
errorCases.response: After prior actor closure, open and fully verify the exact dev receipt/source/bytes and reconcile it under the same manager lease. Record the existing candidate once and resume S1 recovery; a mismatching/incomplete root is candidate-conflict and is never overwritten.
errorCases.userImpact: A completed private publication can be recovered without rebuilding or silently changing identity.

errorCases.scenario: Installed receipt or immutable files are corrupt/ambiguous
errorCases.detection: Bounded receipt parsing finds unknown schema, both receipt modes, mismatched controller delivery/target/source, different inventory/descriptor hash, escaped paths, special files or changed Node/native/control files.
errorCases.response: candidate-conflict/schema-invalid; fail before executing candidate code or quiescing an incumbent. Do not reinterpret a dev receipt as a qualified bundle or rebuild during open/verify.
errorCases.userImpact: Tampering/corruption is visible and does not cause mixed-release execution.

errorCases.scenario: Unsupported predecessor provenance or branch history
errorCases.detection: Selected dev receipt does not match configured source/target/protocol/recipe, or Git ancestry check fails for a requested forward dev upgrade.
errorCases.response: source-incompatible before publication/cutover. No implicit bundle/legacy adoption, branch switch or invented compatibility list.
errorCases.userImpact: Unsupported source transitions require deliberate source-specific handling without data loss.

errorCases.scenario: Required sibling ports or target qualification unavailable
errorCases.detection: Shared manager admission finds missing actual dependency/lifecycle/migration methods, or requested production publication lacks target/native/live qualification.
errorCases.response: Preserve capability-unavailable/target-unqualified. Preparation fixtures may exercise handoff but cannot certify missing owning behavior or enable a platform.
errorCases.userImpact: S2 does not falsely report full live installation, readiness or platform support.

edgeCases.input: Branch moves between read-only check and locked acceptance
edgeCases.expected: offer-stale; no build or state mutation. User accepts a new exact offer explicitly.

edgeCases.input: Branch moves after accepted source is durably recorded
edgeCases.expected: Continue only the recorded commit if obtainable; fetch failure leaves incumbent serving. Recovery never re-resolves the branch.

edgeCases.input: Same source offer already has a verified published release
edgeCases.expected: Reuse it after full identity/inventory/runtime verification. Never rebuild or overwrite different bytes under that release ID.

edgeCases.input: Source contains an ordered hook list or no hook metadata
edgeCases.expected: Validate accepted package.json insrcInstaller metadata, preserve hook order unchanged; absence means zero hooks and does not replace S5's validation.

edgeCases.input: A failed checkout acquires user edits while diagnostics are retained
edgeCases.expected: Retain it and report its location; automated cleanup never deletes edited or ownership-uncertain source.

edgeCases.input: Home/local repository contains spaces or Unicode; Windows drive letter uses another case
edgeCases.expected: Use argument arrays, contained portable relative receipt paths and shared canonical location comparisons. Valid Unicode Git refs are accepted; spaces or other forbidden ref characters are rejected by Git rules.

edgeCases.input: Explicit CUDA setting is empty or another value
edgeCases.expected: Preserve it exactly; default skip only when the variable is absent and record effective value.

edgeCases.input: No npm wrapper exists beside the verified Node executable
edgeCases.expected: Use the absolute matching npm-cli.js for npm ci and coordinator stages; no PATH npm fallback.

edgeCases.input: A worker is admitted but no positive completion/cleanup evidence survives
edgeCases.expected: Remain preparation-uncertain and retain diagnostics; neither a free OS lock nor PID absence authorizes deletion or another worker.

edgeCases.input: An arbitrary build-script descendant starts a new session/group and never registers with the installer/coordinator.
edgeCases.expected: This process is outside the guaranteed ownership boundary. Do not describe empty tracked groups as proof of universal process-tree containment. Scope-boundary test fixtures must explicitly release and confirm their own detached process; known unresolved installer-owned or registered actors remain blocking. User decision limits the guarantee to the owned/cooperating boundary. [[c19]]

invariantsToPreserve.text: HLD public sc1/sc2/sc3/sc5/sc6 wire records and owner boundaries remain unchanged; narrow private S1 composition adaptations are explicit S2 integration work.
S1 remains the sole controller/selection writer. S2 workers do not stop/start daemons, run migration hooks, open app DBs or implement IDE transports.
Terminal-only install, exact accepted offer, immutable candidate verification and selected release bootstrap/runtime TUI handoff remain enforced; all required sibling adapters remain mandatory.
No elevated commands, implicit source/mode switch, daemon PID/signal/kill controls, direct cloud LLM REST or host v2 daemon mutation.
DEF E20261123c3d71313:S002:FR001 and ac1-ac3 apply unchanged. S8 owns real UTM/OrbStack/Windows qualification; local/fixture passes never imply supported production publication.

Cleanup is guaranteed for installer-admitted command actors, retained owned process groups and cooperating registered descendants. Arbitrary unregistered detached processes are outside this guarantee; it is an ownership contract, not process isolation. Known held/unknown owned actors, missing or mismatched registered-actor journals and unsupported tracked-actor disposal evidence remain preparation-uncertain and block publication, retry and cleanup.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test + node:assert/strict with co-located *.test.ts through the canonical coordinator. Owned subprocess fixtures self-exit/control their own lifetimes; host v2 daemon and app stores are untouched. Surrounding tests run per task; the combined installer regression runs after S2 tasks. S2 fixture/local evidence and S8 live platform qualification stay distinct. Cleanup evidence and tests guarantee only installer-admitted actors, retained owned groups and cooperating registered descendants. An unregistered detached process is an explicitly documented scope-boundary fixture, never claimed contained; the fixture must terminate itself and confirm its own teardown.

testLevels.purpose: Strict source/receipt validation and noncircular, mode-specific identity without execution side effects.
fixturesNeeded: Canonical source-offer/dev-receipt vectors; malformed/oversized/unknown-version records; Linux/macOS/Windows path vectors including C:/c: aliases.

testLevels.purpose: Preserve S1 offer/lease/controller/terminal ownership while adding only private dev composition.
fixturesNeeded: Existing manager/controller/terminal fixtures, typed dev adapter, actual ordinary manager subprocess and isolated controller homes; no substitute production sibling implementations.

testLevels.purpose: Exercise real local Git and owned private-tooling preparation, source preservation, failure and recovery. Ownership assertions use the explicit owned/cooperating scope; full staged-file inventory validation is mandatory before prepared.
fixturesNeeded: Two local Git remotes, exact recorded commits, isolated explicit homes/checkouts/stages and nonce-bound worker results.
Owned-process fixtures for manager self-exit, a surviving preparation worker, bounded cancel and confirmed cleanup; missing/foreign cleanup evidence stays blocked.
Command fixtures for unavailable compilers and hostile host Node/npm; fixture success is not target qualification.

Owned/cooperating actor boundary fixture distinguishes tracked held/unknown actors (blocking) from an arbitrary unregistered detached process (outside guarantee); test code releases and confirms its detached fixture before removing temporary data.

Attempt actual foreign-checkpoint admission, retry/cleanup closure guards and retained-data assertions. Missing or tampered non-entrypoint inventory files cannot yield prepared. Full manager retry/deletion integration remains t7.

testLevels.purpose: Probe the implemented private-toolchain and complete payload on the native host, without starting app services or certifying other platforms.
fixturesNeeded: Verified official Node 22.22.1/npm 10.9.4; source checkout helpers run under canonical ownership and explicit npmCli override.
Actual complete payload collection/control bundling/runtime/native probe followed by ordinary manager inspect from a fresh process; publication stays local dev.
Actual UTM macOS/OrbStack Linux/native Windows install/upgrade/migration/IDE acceptance is S8 evidence, not an S2 reported smoke pass.

alternativesConsidered.name: Source offer plus isolated retained checkout
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Resolve a source identity without building, then prepare and publish one verified payload under the existing manager.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Use a private dev-source offer alongside the existing bundle offer, preserving public sc1/sc2 wire records. Under the manager lease, persist accepted source identity before starting an isolated checkout/build. Keep the completed checkout outside immutable payloads as the managed source for later dirty/conflict preflight. Publish a mode-specific dev receipt and complete payload through S1 preparation ownership; reopen without fetch/build. Reuse S1 packaging, runtime and coordinator capabilities with explicit narrow composition edits. The guaranteed cleanup boundary is installer-admitted command actors, retained owned process groups and cooperating registered descendants. Arbitrary unregistered detached processes are outside the guarantee. Known unresolved owned actors remain blocking.
pros: Smallest shape that separates accepted source identity from post-build bytes and preserves read-only checks.
One per-attempt checkout, one receipt and existing controller ownership; no bare cache/worktree registry.
Supports explicit pre-publication recovery and independent immutable payload verification.
cons: Repeated source fetches and retained checkout disk space.
Requires precise private offer/context and installed receipt dispatch integration in existing S1 files.

alternativesConsidered.name: Source offer plus shared bare cache and worktrees
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the same offer/receipt contract but allocate builds from a shared source cache.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Resolve and persist the same source-only offer, use a source-scoped bare Git cache and allocate detached per-operation worktrees, then publish the same complete immutable candidate and dev receipt. Track worktree/cache ownership separately from manager/controller and keep mutable selected sources outside payloads. Lifecycle and migration still use shared owner ports.
pros: Can reuse Git objects across repeated upgrades.
Still preserves source acceptance versus prepared artifact identity and immutable publication.
cons: Adds cache exclusion, linked-worktree path validation and independent cleanup/reference accounting.
More interruption states and shared mutable source state without a correctness requirement for caching.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: The prior alternative adds source preparation machinery unnecessary for the existing S2 mechanics or the user-selected owned/cooperating actor scope; a1 satisfies ac1-ac3 and all consumed shared contracts.

erDefinition.narrative: Shows source intent, serial build attempts and immutable artifacts as distinct records. The manager owns controller/checkpoint writes; each prepared dev release links to its retained mutable checkout without placing that checkout in the runtime inventory. Worker lifetime guarantees apply to installer-admitted and cooperating registered actors; arbitrary unregistered detached processes are outside the ownership model.

DevOperation.description: One existing controller operation that alone coordinates S2 preparation under S1 ownership.

acceptedSource.description: Exactly one accepted source offer; retries cannot replace it.

attempts.description: Zero or more serial owned attempts; never concurrent recovery workers.

candidate.description: Zero or one verified published candidate for this operation.

DevSourceOffer.description: Source identity accepted before output bytes exist.

sourceSha256.description: Canonical source/build-recipe digest, independent of compiled bytes.

checkout.description: Exactly one retained checkout, outside immutable payload.

DevRelease.description: Immutable local dev artifact, verified independently of worker state.

releaseId.description: Prospective source-based release identity fixed before build.

source.description: Exactly one accepted source offer bound by its receipt.

managedCheckout.description: One retained checkout selected by this receipt; code/runtime bytes remain separately inventoried.

descriptorSha256.description: Digest of canonical dev receipt bytes.

inventorySha256.description: Digest of canonical immutable inventory bytes.

ManagedCheckout.description: Mutable source tree retained for exact dirty/conflict preflight; never an installed runtime.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: Separates a read-only source offer from post-consent build output and shows that only the existing manager may publish/controller-record the candidate. The worker's confirmed actor cleanup precedes publication; S1's terminal retains readiness-to-TUI handoff. Cleanup covers installer-admitted command actors, retained owned groups and cooperating registered descendants; no arbitrary descendant isolation is implied.
